name: Monitoring And Alerting Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on monitoring and alerting so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on monitoring and alerting so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Prefer explicit, readable monitoring and alerting solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
2. Keep monitoring and alerting changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Document any non-obvious monitoring and alerting decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. Before starting monitoring and alerting work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to monitoring and alerting (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen monitoring and alerting approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Prefer the simplest monitoring and alerting approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting monitoring and alerting assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic monitoring and alerting advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop monitoring and alerting edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated monitoring and alerting concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these monitoring and alerting guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
